steps.title: Pipeline Anatomy
steps.text: Every pipeline has a PipelineDefinition containing nodes, connections, metadata, and a status lifecycle (Draft, Running, Stopped, Error). Understanding this model is key to building effective pipelines.

steps.title: Node Types and Categories
steps.text: Surgewave pipelines support 6 node categories: Source nodes (Generator, Topic, File), Sink nodes (Stdio, Topic, Database), Transform nodes (SQL, Filter, Map), AI/ML nodes (Embedding, LLM, RAG), Streams nodes, and Workflow nodes.

steps.title: Workflow Patterns
steps.text: Workflow nodes enable advanced patterns: human-in-the-loop approval gates, batch processing with configurable windows, conditional routing based on content, retry loops for transient failures, and stateful processing.

steps.title: Building a RAG Pipeline
steps.text: Lesson 34.4 walks you through building a RAG chatbot pipeline with 7 nodes: Topic Source, Document Chunker, Embedding Generator, Vector Store, Retriever, LLM Prompt Builder, and Chat Endpoint.

steps.title: Pipeline Chat API
steps.text: Lesson 34.7 covers the Pipeline Chat API for real-time conversational AI. Chat-enabled pipelines support session management, SSE streaming for token-by-token delivery, and a ChatDrawer UI component.
